title: Native Modules and Platform APIs
description: Understand how to extend React Native apps by using native modules and accessing platform-specific APIs to unlock device features.

lessons.title: What are Native Modules?
lessons.content: Native modules let you write platform-specific code (Java/Kotlin for Android, Objective-C/Swift for iOS) to access features not available in React Native by default.

lessons.title: When to Use Native Modules
lessons.content: Use native modules when you need advanced device capabilities like sensors, background services, or custom UI elements that React Native doesn’t provide out-of-the-box.

lessons.title: How Native Modules Work with React Native
lessons.content: React Native bridges JavaScript and native code using a communication layer. Native modules expose functions to JS, and JS can call them asynchronously.

lessons.title: Using Existing Native Modules
Creating a Simple Native Module (Android)
Creating a Simple Native Module (iOS)
Calling Native Module Methods from JS
Accessing Platform APIs with React Native
lessons.content: React Native provides APIs for common platform features like Camera, Location, Sensors, and Push Notifications via native modules, often wrapped in JavaScript.

lessons.title: Permissions in React Native
lessons.content: Many native features require user permissions. Use `react-native-permissions` or built-in APIs to request and check permissions at runtime for both Android and iOS.

lessons.title: Best Practices for Native Modules
lessons.content:
- Keep native module logic simple and focused
- Handle errors gracefully and inform JS side
- Document native APIs clearly
- Test on both Android and iOS devices
- Use community libraries when possible to save time
